principles: Traditional Catholic spiritual formation for ordinary users, not a seminary ascetical-theology textbook.
Every explanatory claim has explicit provenance.
Doctrine, current discipline, traditional counsel, school-specific method and product guidance remain distinguishable.
Prayer texts and devotional execution remain in PRAY; sacramental execution remains with their canonical owners.
No invented prayers, AI-generated meditations or synthetic spiritual methods.
No gamification, streaks, rankings, holiness scores or sin ledgers.
Methods must be adapted to state of life and circumstances; duties of state outrank optional exercises when they conflict.
Advanced mystical phenomena, visions, infused-state taxonomy, priest/religious-specific formation and scruples are outside the core course.
source_hierarchy: Sacred Scripture and doctrinal/catechetical owners control doctrine.
Papal magisterium and canon law control reparation/indulgence doctrine and current discipline.
Tanquerey is the principal traditional synthetic spine and locator map.
St Francis de Sales is the principal lay-facing control for prayer, adaptation, dryness and spiritual reading.
St Ignatius controls the examen methods.
Chautard contributes the prayer/action relationship only.

stages.objective: Understand what spiritual growth is for and why it is not reserved to clergy or religious.

claims.text: Christian perfection is ordered to love of God, union with Him and conformity to His will rather than the accumulation of devotional activities.
The devout life must be adapted to a person's state and duties rather than copied mechanically from another vocation.
The desire for spiritual progress should be calm, persevering and grace-dependent rather than impatient or presumptuous.
Methods, exercises and schedules are means to union with God; they are not the end of the spiritual life.
The app must not turn holiness into points, streaks, ranks or visible spiritual-performance scoring.

stages.objective: Learn recollection and the presence of God as a simple, repeatable orientation of the day.

claims.text: The practice of the presence of God rests on God's omnipresence and, in the supernatural order, on His indwelling in the soul by grace.
Frequent affectionate remembrance of God can prolong the fruit of mental prayer through the day.
Recollection is compatible with ordinary work and duties; it does not require constant withdrawal from action.
Presence of God is not a technique for suppressing thought but an act of faith, attention and love.
Short aspirations and renewed intentions can restore recollection when attention has been dispersed.

stages.objective: Understand mental prayer before learning a particular method.

claims.text: Mental prayer is interior intercourse with God involving the mind and heart and ordered to union with Him.
Meditation should move beyond analysis toward affections, prayer and practical resolution.
Meditation on the life and Passion of Christ is a privileged school of imitation and love.
Methodical meditation is a guide for prayer, not the only possible form of mental prayer.
Beginners can start through meditative reading: read a short solid passage, consider its truth, examine personal application, resolve concretely and ask for grace.
Formation may teach a method, but the actual act of prayer must not become a scripted AI-generated pseudo-meditation.
Vocal and mental prayer are not rivals: vocal prayer can awaken interior devotion, while mental prayer can deepen attention to the words being prayed.

stages.objective: Learn one traditional Christ-centred method without mistaking it for a universal obligation.

claims.text: The Saint-Sulpice method is one traditional method among several; it is not the universal definition of mental prayer.
Its central movement is Christ before the eyes, in the heart and in the hands.
Jesus before the eyes means considering Christ as model and rendering Him adoration and homage.
Jesus in the heart means seeking through prayer to receive and share His dispositions and virtues.
Jesus in the hands means practical co-operation: carrying the received light into concrete action and resolution.
As prayer matures, the method should serve loving attention to God rather than become a rigid checklist of acts.

stages.objective: Remove the idea that prayer has failed whenever it feels distracted or dry.

claims.text: The absence of sensible consolation does not make prayer useless or failed.
During dryness one should remain peacefully faithful rather than abandon prayer merely because it feels barren.
Vocal prayer, attentive spiritual reading, a crucifix or a simple act of recollection can help when the mind is scattered.
When duties genuinely prevent the usual prayer period, the response should be prudent adaptation rather than anxiety or self-condemnation.
The app must not infer spiritual regression from missed sessions, lack of consolation or reduced prayer duration.

stages.objective: Learn a calm daily review distinct from sacramental Confession preparation.

claims.text: The general examen reviews the day in God's presence in order to know oneself, give thanks, repent and amend.
Its classical five movements are thanksgiving, asking light, reviewing the day, asking pardon and resolving amendment with grace.
A daily general examen is not identical to the fuller examination made in immediate preparation for sacramental Confession.
The purpose of examination is reform and renewed dependence on grace, not anxious self-surveillance.
The app must keep examen finite and calm and must not retain a private ledger of sins as a spiritual-performance record.

stages.objective: Learn how focused work on one fault or virtue differs from the general examen.

claims.text: The particular examen focuses on one definite fault to correct or virtue to cultivate rather than reviewing every aspect of the day.
A focused examination can make practical resolutions more concrete and easier to test in ordinary situations.
Traditional counting marks are a tool of one method, not a requirement and not a spiritual score.
A chosen point should be sufficiently specific to guide action, such as guarding speech in a recurring situation or practising a particular virtue.
The point may change as needs change; persistence is not the same as rigid attachment to one exercise.
If the app offers a particular-examen aid, data should be minimal and private and should not create charts that invite vanity, anxiety or scrupulous comparison.

stages.objective: Learn to read for prayer and conversion rather than merely to accumulate religious information.

claims.text: The purpose of spiritual reading is to nourish prayer, convictions and practical Christian life.
Spiritual reading should normally be slow and attentive enough for a truth to be considered, relished and applied.
Sacred Scripture, sound spiritual works and suitable lives of saints are traditional sources for spiritual reading.
Not everything admirable in a saint's life is directly imitable in every state of life; application must respect circumstances and vocation.
Formation should teach selection and method but should not substitute endless content consumption for prayer and practice.

stages.objective: Connect prayer with work, family duties and ordinary actions without importing a narrow school-specific spirituality.

claims.text: Ordinary lawful actions can be directed to God's glory and performed in union with Christ.
The duties of one's state are not interruptions of spiritual life; faithfully performed, they are material for sanctification.
A brief supernatural intention before important actions can help unite work to prayer without requiring continuous conscious verbal prayer.
The spiritual life should make a person more faithful to real duties, charity and responsibilities, not less available to them.
No single modern movement owns the doctrine of sanctifying ordinary duties; the course presents it as broad Catholic tradition.

title.en: A Rule of Life Without Rigidity
title.fr: Une règle de vie sans rigidité

stages.objective: Build a stable spiritual rhythm that serves duties and adapts prudently to circumstances.

claims.text: A rule of life can help order time, spiritual exercises, duties and the practice of virtue.
A good rule must be firm enough to sustain consistency and flexible enough to adapt to real circumstances.
Duties should be graded by importance; urgent charity or a more necessary duty may rightly displace a nonessential exercise.
A small stable core is preferable to an elaborate programme that repeatedly collapses under work, family, illness or travel.
A rule of life should be reviewed when state, health, work or family circumstances materially change.
Ad Orientem may help a user understand or sketch a rule, but it must not become a generic life-planner or treat every optional devotion as a required task.

stages.objective: Learn why apostolic activity and good works must remain rooted in the interior life.

claims.text: External activity is not a substitute for prayer and interior union with Christ.
For active Catholics, prayer should sustain purity of intention, dependence on grace and perseverance in good works.
The busier a person becomes in apostolic work, the more important it is to preserve the essentials of interior life rather than allow activity to consume them.
This lesson does not teach Apostolate technique; Apostolate remains the owner of helping, teaching and answering others.
The fruit sought is not inactivity but action that proceeds from prayer and returns a person to deeper union with God.

stages.objective: Understand these practices without reducing them to a transaction or points economy.

claims.text: Reparation is a real Catholic response of love, justice and union with Christ, not a mechanism for earning spiritual points.
An indulgence is remission before God of temporal punishment for sins whose guilt has already been forgiven.
Current discipline distinguishes partial and plenary indulgences and establishes conditions for gaining a plenary indulgence.
Older days/years terminology is not the current measure and did not mean a literal number of days removed from Purgatory.
Formation explains indulgences and reparation; Calendar and PRAY may surface specific opportunities or prayers when they have their own verified grants.
The app must never display indulgences, reparatory acts or devotions as a score, balance, streak or guaranteed exchange.

stages.objective: Distinguish Catholic devotion from magical or automatic thinking.

claims.text: Superstition includes attributing supernatural efficacy to an action or object that it does not possess according to the Church's teaching and practice.
External devotion must remain ordered to interior faith, worship and conversion rather than functioning as an independent mechanism.
Sacramentals and devotional objects should lead toward prayer and Christian life, not replace them.
Claims of guaranteed worldly success or salvation from mere possession or mechanical use of an object require correction unless a genuine Church promise is accurately stated.
Customs and sacramentals remain owned by their dedicated reference/PRAY/Customary surfaces; Spiritual Life teaches the interior principle only.

stages.objective: Integrate prayer, examen, reading and duties without overload or spiritual self-measurement.

claims.text: A mature spiritual rhythm integrates prayer, duties, sacraments, reading and self-examination rather than multiplying practices without order.
Growth may require simplification and deeper attention rather than adding more devotions.
Spiritual exercises should be adapted to real capacity and circumstances while preserving fidelity to essential duties.
Formation gives principles and methods but does not replace a confessor or spiritual director in matters requiring personal discernment.
The desired product outcome is greater freedom for prayerful Catholic life, not dependence on the app for every spiritual action.
